content: checkWarrenConfig (src/diagnostics/checks.ts) emits a single 'warren_config' check that walks every registered project, parsing each .warren/ via the cache when supplied (cache?: WarrenConfigCache) or directly via load() (tests). Empty project list -> ok with 'no projects registered'. WarrenConfigUnavailableError on a project becomes a per-project failure entry rather than throwing past the check; per-file errors are aggregated as '<projectId> <file>: <message>' joined with '; '. Hint always points at /projects/:id/refresh.

checkBurrowPoolReachable (src/diagnostics/checks.ts, warren-c0c9) is the /readyz-side burrow probe — aggregates BurrowClientPool.probe() across every registered worker and degrades to a single `{ok: false, message}` envelope listing failing workers by name. The single-client checkBurrowReachable stays for `warren doctor` (env-derived BurrowClient, not a pool).

checkWarrenDb (src/diagnostics/checks.ts, warren-e2ea) is pure env→DiagnosticCheck: parses WARREN_DB_URL (or synthesizes from legacy WARREN_DB_PATH) via parseDatabaseUrl and reports the dialect on success ('sqlite <path>' or 'postgres'). Surfaces three failures: malformed URL (ValidationError from parseDatabaseUrl), WARREN_DB_URL/WARREN_DB_PATH disagree (sqliteUrlForPath(path) !== url), and the empty sentinel. checkDatabaseReachable (also in checks.ts) is the live SELECT-1 probe: takes an optional AnyWarrenDb (degrades to ok=true 'no db handle wired' when absent so tests can omit the seam), runs pingDatabase(db), and reports 'dialect=sqlite'|'dialect=postgres' on success. Both wired into warren doctor (after the CANOPY_REPO_URL check) and /readyz (as the first probe before the burrow pool fan-out).

checkPreviewPortAllocator (src/diagnostics/checks.ts, warren-2277) takes a { probe: { usage() } } seam rather than a db handle directly — both warren doctor and /readyz construct a PreviewPortAllocator from deps.db and pass it as the probe, while tests stub a fake usage() so the threshold logic can be exercised without a live db. Returns ok=false at saturation ≥ warnRatio (default PREVIEW_PORT_USAGE_WARN_RATIO=0.8). The hint names BOTH WARREN_PREVIEW_PORT_RANGE and the TTL knobs (WARREN_PREVIEW_IDLE_TTL / WARREN_PREVIEW_MAX_LIFETIME) so operators know either widening the range or tightening eviction is a valid fix. A zero-total range collapses to ratio=1 to avoid NaN. Server-side wiring threads ServerDeps.previewPortRange (resolved from WARREN_PREVIEW_PORT_RANGE at boot in src/server/main.ts) so /readyz doesn't re-parse env per request.

checkPreviewAuthStrength (src/diagnostics/checks.ts, warren-8a10) warns when WARREN_PREVIEW_HOST is set but WARREN_API_TOKEN matches a known placeholder (changeme/placeholder/warren-token/your-token-here/insecure/secret) or is shorter than PREVIEW_MIN_TOKEN_LENGTH (16 chars). Wired into both /readyz (src/server/handlers.ts) and warren doctor (src/cli/commands/doctor.ts). No-op when WARREN_PREVIEW_HOST is absent.

checkWarrenConfigDeprecations (src/diagnostics/checks.ts, warren-5840) is the informational counterpart to checkWarrenConfig: walks the same projects, surfaces LoadedWarrenConfig.warnings[] in a 'warren_config_deprecations' row, and stays ok=true regardless so legacy installs don't flip warren doctor / readyz red. Skips projects whose load threw (those are surfaced by checkWarrenConfig). Wired into doctor.ts after checkWarrenConfig and into the /readyz handler in handlers.ts alongside it.

src/diagnostics/redact.ts is the single place a diagnostics check converts an unvetted failure into a wire-safe reason code (classifyDbFailure -> unreachable|auth_failed|migration_pending|unknown). DiagnosticCheck.message is rendered verbatim by /readyz, so no check may interpolate driver text, absolute paths, or secret lengths.
